benchmark_name: Benchmarking Vision-Language and Multimodal Large Language Models on Christian Iconography (ArtDL, ICONCLASS, Wikidata saint classification)
humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark targets iconographic classification of Christian saints using Iconclass codes, an art-historical competence, rather than using art images as generic classification material.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Paintings (images) are paired with text prompts listing class labels or Iconclass descriptions; few-shot adds exemplar images with labels. The CSV metadata lists text only, but the images are the primary input.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label classification of Christian saints in paintings (10 most frequent Iconclass classes per dataset), framed by the authors as 'iconographic classification' under zero-shot with labels, zero-shot with Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot with five exemplars.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task (single-label classification of Christian saints) in one domain.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, plus CLIP and SigLIP variants and ResNet50 baselines.

summary: The paper benchmarks CLIP/SigLIP and multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5) on single-label classification of Christian saints across three Iconclass-annotated datasets, under zero-shot, zero-shot with descriptions, and few-shot conditions. Results are compared against fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines. Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o beat the baselines on ArtDL and ICONCLASS but not on Wikidata.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5 Pro peaked at 90.45% on ArtDL; SigLIP-so400m was best on Wikidata (66.29%). Class descriptions generally helped zero-shot performance; few-shot mostly lowered accuracy. LLMs showed low cross-dataset consistency (25-33%) compared with contrastive models. Possible training-data contamination for ArtDL and ICONCLASS is noted.
facets_explanation: The paper does not describe a new annotation process: labels are the Iconclass codes already attached to images in ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set and Wikidata, filtered to single-label images of the top 10 saint classes. The Introduction says only generically that such corpora carry metadata 'usually created by domain experts', so existing_metadata is chosen as the closest value (labels lifted from existing records), not on the basis of a stated annotator description. In Test 1 the model sees only the label names, so naming the saint from the painting relies on knowledge outside the image and candidate list. Test 2 supplies Iconclass descriptions in the prompt, which partly reduces this. Scoring is top-1 match to the single Iconclass label.
results_explanation: Headline score: Table 2 gives 'gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 90.45% 90.18% 86.59%' on ArtDL, so the best accuracy is 90.45% (Test 1). I recomputed all within-model, within-dataset differences across Tests 1-3 in Tables 2-4. The maximum is siglip-base-patch16-512 on ArtDL, 'siglip-base-patch16-512 48.71% 68.19% 55.90%': Test 2 minus Test 1 = 68.19 - 48.71 = 19.48, rounded down to the integer 19. The next largest are siglip-large-patch16-384 on ArtDL (72.21 vs 53.49, 18.72) and on Wikidata (61.17 vs 43.95, 17.22); the largest ICONCLASS gap is siglip-large 49.30 vs 38.77 (10.53). The earlier value 21 was wrong. No human baseline is reported, so the human fields are null.

dataset_size.quote: The test set, published along with the paper, contains 1,864 images.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Models were tested under three conditions: (1) classification using class labels, (2) classification with Iconclass descriptions, and (3) few-shot learning with five exemplars.

gold_source.quote: Each image is annotated with Iconclass codes, covering 10 key figures of Christian iconography
usually created by domain experts, that describes the general content of the images

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: The models classify images using only class label names
This configuration tests the model’s ability to leverage pre-trained knowledge connections between visual features and semantic concepts.

answer_multiplicity.quote: Each is mapped to a single iconographic label
